Mercedes-Benz Finland  ·  SEO, Content & Performance Audit

Report v2.0 · 18 May 2026
3 URLs · 6 Lighthouse runs
Verified — real measurements

This is a verified audit. Data captured via Playwright + Lighthouse 12 against the live site on 18 May 2026. Screenshots are the actual rendered pages. Numbers are real.

Scope

Landing
https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/
Model index (redirected from e-class)
https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/models/
ECO-huolto service
https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/services/eco-huolto/

Executive Summary

Desktop is strong. Mobile is broken.

All three pages render well on desktop (Lighthouse Performance 93–96), but the mobile experience collapses: the landing page takes 12.3 seconds to its Largest Contentful Paint on a throttled 4G device, and ECO-huolto takes 10.6 s. Total blocking time on the landing page is 1.78 s — the user's thumb is locked out for nearly two seconds. The cause is concentrated and fixable: ~1.5 MB of render-blocking JavaScript and CSS shipped to mobile clients, most of it served from cloudfront.net (Adobe AEM clientlibs) and never used on first paint.

On‑page SEO is good in the basics (Finnish titles & descriptions, self-canonical, lang="fi-FI"), but breaks down in structure: no <h1> on the model index or service page, zero <h2>/<h3> across all three pages, no Schema.org JSON-LD anywhere, and no hreflang. Image accessibility is poor: 59 % of images on the model index are missing alt; 49 % on the service page.

Top 8 fixes (do these first)

FIX-01P0Verified
Mobile LCP is 12.3 s on the landing page (Lighthouse Perf 31/100)

Lab measurement on a simulated 4G handset. The LCP element is the hero image img.lcp-image (1922 × 875), already correctly tagged fetchpriority="high" — but it sits behind ~1.5 MB of render-blocking script and is decoded only after main-thread is freed.

Top blocker: cloudfront.net (Adobe AEM clientlibs) — 702 KB transferred, 1,833 ms of main-thread blocking time on mobile.
Unused JavaScript savings: 1,540 ms reported by Lighthouse for the landing page; 1,240 ms on ECO-huolto.

Do:

1. Split the AEM clientlib bundle: ship only "above-the-fold" CSS/JS in head;
   lazy-load the rest behind requestIdleCallback or on first-scroll.
2. Move the Cookiebot script (currently 112-137 KB, 497 ms blocking) to async,
   reserve banner footprint in CSS so consent does not retrigger layout.
3. Drop the 79 third-party <script> tags on the landing page to < 25
   by consolidating duplicate trackers (Adobe Analytics + GTM + Floodlight overlap).
4. Preload the hero image only once (currently fetched twice via clientlib + img tag).
FIX-02P0Verified
Heading hierarchy is broken on every page
Landing: single <h1> reading "Meistä" (an "About us" tile, not the homepage proposition). 0 <h2>, 0 <h3>.
Model index: 0 <h1>, 0 <h2>, 0 <h3>.
ECO-huolto: 0 <h1>, 0 <h2>, 0 <h3>.

Lighthouse confirms heading-order failing (score 0.00) on all three pages. Search engines and screen-readers both rely on this skeleton; missing it leaves the page's main topic to be inferred from the title alone.

Do: Put one descriptive <h1> on every page (homepage: a brand+market line; model index: "Mercedes-Benz mallisto"; service page: "Mercedes-Benz ECO-huolto"). Convert AEM section headlines from <div class="headline"> to <h2>/<h3> in a sequential order. Zero design change.

FIX-03P0Verified
76 of 197 images are missing alt text (39 %)
Landing 18 / 92 missing — Model index 38 / 64 (59 %) — ECO-huolto 20 / 41 (49 %).
Lighthouse image-alt = 0.00 on landing and service. The LCP image itself ships with alt="" (decorative declaration), which is defensible for a hero — but most missing alts are on content images, not hero.

Do: AEM ships alt as a required field for content images; turn the validation on. Author guideline: Finnish, ≤ 125 chars, describe the subject not the file ("Mercedes-Benz EQE matkalla saaristossa", not "hero-eqe-1.jpg").

FIX-04P0Verified
No Schema.org JSON-LD on any page

Captured DOM contains zero application/ld+json blocks with a parsed @type. For an OEM site this is the single biggest "free" SERP feature unlock.

Do: add to the global head template:

<script type="application/ld+json">{
  "@context":"https://schema.org",
  "@type":"AutomotiveBusiness",
  "name":"Mercedes-Benz Suomi",
  "url":"https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/",
  "logo":"https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/.../logo.svg",
  "sameAs":["https://www.facebook.com/MercedesBenzSuomi", "..."]
}</script>

Model pages: add Vehicle with brand, model, vehicleEngine, offers.price (EUR). Service page: add Service + FAQPage. Roughly 25 lines per template, no design impact.

FIX-05P0Verified
hreflang is missing on every page
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="…"> count: 0 on landing, model, and service.

Without this, Google guesses between mercedes-benz.fi, .se, .com when serving Finnish queries — and the canonical site sometimes loses to the .com fallback.

<link rel="alternate" hreflang="fi-FI"    href="https://www.mercedes-benz.fi/{path}" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://www.mercedes-benz.com/{path}" />

Inject from the AEM page template; verify reciprocity on the global side.

FIX-06P1Verified
147 empty-text links on the landing page
Landing 147 / 576 anchors with no accessible name — model index 130 / 508 — ECO-huolto 120 / 356.
Lighthouse link-name = 0.00 on all three pages.

Most are icon-only navigation chevrons and social buttons. Each one is invisible to screen-readers and crawler anchor-text graphs.

Do: add aria-label="…" to every icon-only <a>. Use the existing global icon set's name map — this is a single component change in AEM.

FIX-07P1Verified
e-class.html → /models/ redirect costs 853 ms

The historical model URL still exists in external backlinks and Google's index. Each user hitting it pays 853 ms (Lighthouse redirects opportunity) before the new URL even begins to load.

Do: serve the legacy URL with a direct 301 to the actual E-Class page (or to /models/saloon/e-class/, whichever you settled on), not via a soft client-side bounce. Then update sitemap.xml so Google drops the legacy URL.

FIX-08P1Verified
Browser console errors on every page

Lighthouse errors-in-console = 0.00 on all three pages. JS errors directly impact perceived quality and Core Web Vitals (failed scripts can leave layout in intermediate states). Open DevTools on each page, fix the throwing scripts, add a CI check that fails the build on new console errors via Playwright.

Specific actions for the landing page

  1. Replace the <h1>"Meistä" with an evergreen Finnish line: "Mercedes-Benz Suomi — uudet ja käytetyt autot, hyötyajoneuvot ja huolto."
  2. Add 4-6 sequential <h2> headings on the section tiles (Mallisto, Tarjoukset, Käytetyt, Huolto, Lataus, Jälleenmyyjät) — replaces the current heading-less divs with no visual change.
  3. Defer all non-essential scripts: Cookiebot to async + early consent flow, GTM bootstrap to first-interaction, Adobe Target to after-LCP.
  4. Audit the 32 eagerly-loaded images above the fold — only the hero needs fetchpriority="high"; the rest should be loading="lazy".

Specific actions for the model index

  1. The 853 ms redirect from /passengercars/models/saloon/e-class.html is a real user cost — switch to a direct 301 and prune the legacy URL from sitemap.xml.
  2. Add an <h1>Mercedes-Benz mallisto</h1> at the top of the grid.
  3. 59 % missing alt is the worst of the three pages — model tile images are the most-shared assets in social previews; alt text doubles as Twitter/OG fallback.
  4. Meta description is too short (64 chars); aim for 140–160 with a clear CTA verb ("Vertaile mallistoa, varaa koeajo.").

Specific actions for ECO-huolto

  1. LCP 10.6 s on mobile makes this the slowest of the three pages. Same root cause: render-blocking AEM clientlibs.
  2. This is a high-intent service page (older-car owner looking for a service quote). Add FAQPage JSON-LD with 5 Finnish questions (mitä kuuluu hintaan / soveltuvat mallit / kesto / varaosa-takuu / varauslomake) — rich-results eligibility is almost automatic.
  3. Add <h1>ECO-huolto</h1> and a clear price-from line in the hero (currently buried).
  4. Expose dealer locator above the fold — this is the conversion path for the page.

Methodology & reproducibility

All findings tagged Verified are derived from one of:

  • audit/data/summary.json — Playwright DOM extract (titles, meta, headings, hreflang, JSON-LD, image alt, anchor text, navigation/paint timings).
  • audit/lighthouse/*.report.{json,html} — six Lighthouse 12 runs (3 URLs × mobile + desktop, simulated 4G / cable).
  • audit/screens/*.png — nine full-page screenshots (3 URLs × 3 viewports).

Re-run from the GitHub repo with Actions → MB Finland audit → Run workflow. The job captures fresh data into the same paths and commits them to claude/seo-content-audit-3yIo0. To regenerate this report against new data, ask Claude to "rebuild the audit report from the captured data".
